disease_info: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder characterized by disturbances in thought, perception, and behavior, including delusions, hallucinations, disorganized thinking, and negative symptoms such as diminished motivation and emotional expression. Onset typically occurs in late adolescence or early adulthood, but later-life onset and relapses can occur, with a course that ranges from episodic to progressively deteriorating. Functional impairment in work, relationships, and self-care is common, often persisting beyond acute episodes if negative symptoms or cognitive deficits are prominent. It is differentiated from mood and substance-induced psychotic disorders by the relative independence of psychotic symptoms from mood episodes and the absence of a direct physiological cause.

narrative.stressor: About two and a half years ago, Bruce took on a high-stakes consulting contract modeling water-use scenarios for a regional agency, coinciding with a major software migration at his firm and tighter-than-usual deadlines. Initially he responded by leaning into his usual habits of late-night puzzle marathons and meticulous spreadsheet checks, but colleagues noticed that his quality control reviews began taking him far longer and he increasingly resisted collaborating, insisting on redoing work that had already been signed off. Over the next two years, he became less reliable at mentoring junior analysts, missed early-morning hikes with the Trailblazers club, and started declining invitations to star-gazing meet-ups, as his preoccupation with certain project data and interpretations crowded out his previous balance of work and leisure. The situation came to a head when he repeatedly clashed with a client over what they saw as unfounded concerns in the model outputs, and his spouse, alarmed by the impact on his job and their home life, persuaded him to see a psychiatrist after his firm suggested a leave of absence.
narrative.chief_complaint: “I’m here because I’m absolutely certain there are serious problems and hidden manipulations in the data at work, but no one believes me and it’s starting to cost me my job.”

narrative.stressor: Keshia’s difficulties began shortly after high school graduation, when her close friends left Cordova for college or jobs elsewhere and she stayed behind, planning to apply for administrative positions at the local healthcare clinic. Without the structure of school and youth group activities, she leaned heavily on her solitary routines—gardening, knitting, and journaling—but her family noticed that she gradually withdrew from church events and stopped following through on job applications, despite talking about them in detail. Over the next two years, her days became increasingly narrowed to repetitive, highly structured home activities, and she avoided even low-key social gatherings she once enjoyed, like community center yoga or watching the minor-league baseball games with relatives. Her mother finally encouraged an evaluation when Keshia abandoned an internship at the clinic after only a few days, explaining vaguely that she felt "too shut down" to talk to people or keep up with the work, and spending most of her time alone in her room.
narrative.chief_complaint: “I feel like I’ve lost the drive to do anything or be around people, and it’s getting harder and harder to talk or care about things the way I used to.”

narrative.stressor: Around two years ago, Brent was in the middle of expanding his boutique financial advisory practice when he went through a tumultuous breakup with a long-term partner who had been deeply involved in his social and arts circles. In the months that followed, he threw himself into work and the Cincinnati arts scene, but colleagues and family noticed he became increasingly preoccupied with certain clients and local art patrons, interpreting minor business setbacks and awkward social interactions as part of a broader pattern of people working against him. Over time this preoccupation began to erode his easy rapport with clients; he canceled meetings at the last minute, dropped out of his usual pick-up basketball games, and cut short trips he had meticulously planned, saying he didn’t feel safe or welcome. His sister ultimately pushed him to see a psychiatrist after he confided to her that he was convinced specific people in his professional and art networks were secretly coordinating to undermine his reputation and practice, despite repeated reassurances and lack of concrete evidence.
narrative.chief_complaint: “I’m convinced certain people in my professional and art circles are secretly working together to damage my reputation and my practice, even though everyone keeps telling me it’s not really happening.”
